+**Theorem 6.1 (Two-family squeeze with additive error $O(1/a)$).** Fix $0<\lambda_-\le\lambda_+<\infty$. There are $A,C$, depending only on this interval, such that for all integers $a\ge A$ and $\delta=\lambda/a$ with $\lambda\in[\lambda_-,\lambda_+]$, put
+
+$$
+T=\frac\delta a=\frac\lambda{a^2},\qquad
+H_{\rm rare}=\frac1T+\frac{r^3}{1-T}.
+\tag{6.1}
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+\boxed{\quad
+\min\{H_{\rm dense},H_{\rm rare}\}-\frac Ca
+\le\inf_x H(x)\le\min\{H_{\rm dense},H_{\rm rare}\}.
+\quad}\tag{6.2}
+$$
+
+The rare value is the energy of the actual law $x_{\{e\}}=T$, $x_C=1-T$. Every law with $t<t_{\rm conv}$ satisfies the exact lower bound $H\ge H_{\rm rare}$ for all these parameters once $a\ge A$. The theorem does not identify the exact global dense minimizer or an exact finite-$a$ transition.
+
+**Proof.** The upper bounds are the two laws of Lemma 1.2; at $t=T$, the missing-one masses in (1.4) vanish and the full-core mass is $1-T$, proving (6.1).
+
+For the lower bound, a law with $H>H_{\rm dense}+1$ already exceeds the proposed minimum. On the remaining sublevel $H\le H_{\rm dense}+1$, a law with $t\ge t_{\rm conv}$ satisfies (3.2). Its error is at most $C\delta\le C\lambda_+/a$, proving the desired dense-branch lower bound.
+
+Consider now $t<t_{\rm conv}$. Uniformly on the fixed interval of $\lambda$,
+
+$$
+t<t_{\rm conv}=O(a^{-2}),\qquad
+\sum_{i\in C}(1-y_i)=\delta+t=O(a^{-1}),\qquad
+\min_{i\in C}y_i\ge1-\delta-t.
+\tag{6.3}
+$$
+
+On the energy sublevel just specified, (5.14) and
+$H_{\rm dense}-q^3=O(a^2)$ give
+
+$$
+m^2(1/t-t)\le O(a^2),\qquad m^2=O(1).
+$$
+
+This conditional-moment estimate uses that sublevel; the scalar comparison that follows in fact needs no bound on $m$ or on $H$.
+
+Choose a fixed $C_1$ large enough that both $t_{\rm conv}$ and $T$ are at most $C_1/a^2$ for all the parameters in question. By (1.2), $g_\theta'>0$ on $(0,q)$ and $g_\theta'(t)=O(a^3)$ uniformly on $0<t\le C_1/a^2$. Hence
+
+$$
+h_\theta'(t)=-1/t^2+g_\theta'(t)<0
+\quad(0<t\le C_1/a^2)
+\tag{6.4}
+$$
+
+for all sufficiently large $a$ depending only on $\lambda_+$. Also
+$\Lambda_\theta(t)=O(a)$ on this interval, and $1/t\ge a^2/C_1$.
+
+If $t\le T$, monotonicity (6.4) and (2.6) give
+
+$$
+H\ge h_\theta(T)+v\left[\frac1t-\frac{\Lambda_\theta(t)}3\right]
+\ge h_\theta(T),
+$$
+
+because $v\ge0$ and the bracket is positive for all sufficiently large $a$. If $t\ge T$, the increase of $g_\theta$ gives
+
+$$
+h_\theta(t)\ge h_\theta(T)+\frac1t-\frac1T.
+$$
+
+The exact capacity and $r=a+1$ imply
+
+$$
+\frac1t-\frac1T\ge-\frac{\mu-1}{\delta}
+\ge-\frac v{3\delta}.
+\tag{6.5}
+$$
+
+Therefore the second line of (2.6) yields
+
+$$
+H\ge h_\theta(T)+v\left[
+\frac1t-\frac1{3\delta}-\frac{\Lambda_\theta(t)}3\right]
+\ge h_\theta(T).\tag{6.6}
+$$
+
+Indeed $1/(3\delta)\le a/(3\lambda_-)$ and $\Lambda_\theta(t)=O(a)$, whereas $1/t\ge a^2/C_1$. This positivity is uniform on the given compact interval. Since $h_\theta(T)=H_{\rm rare}$, both rare cases give the exact bound. They did not use the preliminary sublevel restriction, so it can be dropped for the last assertion of the theorem. Combining the dense and rare branches, together with the trivial high-energy case, proves (6.2). ∎
+

+**Proposition 7.3 (An explicit counterlaw for every $a\ge7$).** At
+
+$$
+\delta=\frac1{2a},\qquad
+\varepsilon=\frac{(2r-1)\delta}{r^2},\tag{7.6}
+$$
+
+the law (7.2) is feasible and satisfies
+
+$$
+H_d-\mathcal H(\varepsilon)
+\ge\frac{(2r-1)^2\delta^2}{r^2\mu^3}>0.\tag{7.7}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** The strict mass inequality in (7.3) is equivalent to
+
+$$
+(2a+1)(a+2)<(a-1)(a+1)^2.
+$$
+
+The difference is $a^3-a^2-6a-3$, positive for $a\ge7$ since it is at least $6a^2-6a-3$. Also $\varepsilon<1/(ar)$ and $\mu\ge7/9$. For every $0\le z\le\varepsilon$ these imply
+
+$$
+\mu-\frac{2z}{a}\ge\frac9{10}\mu>0,
+$$
+
+because $2/(a^2r)\le2/(7^2\cdot8)<7/90\le\mu/10$. Direct differentiation of (7.4) gives
+
+$$
+\mathcal H''(z)
+=\frac{4r^2}{(\mu+z)^3}
+ +\frac{8r^2}{a(\mu-2z/a)^3}
+ -\frac{24(2r-1)\delta}{a(\mu-2z/a)^4}
+\le\frac{6r^2}{\mu^3}.
+$$
+
+The last step uses $8/[a(9/10)^3]\le2$ for $a\ge7$. Taylor's theorem and (7.5) now yield
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathcal H(\varepsilon)-H_d
+&\le-\frac{4(2r-1)\delta\varepsilon}{\mu^3}
+ +\frac{3r^2\varepsilon^2}{\mu^3}\\
+&=-\frac{(2r-1)^2\delta^2}{r^2\mu^3}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+This proves both feasibility and strict improvement. ∎
+

+## 6. Unresolved global values
+
+**Open problem 6.1 (Ratios outside the matching set).** For $\kappa\in(0,\infty)\setminus\{2,4,6,\ldots\}$, determine whether $D_n$ converges along every sequence (1.2), whether its limit is independent of that sequence, and, if so, its value. Theorems 4.2 and 4.4 establish only the bounds (4.2) and the exact values at positive even ratios. The parameter regime (1.2) has fixed positive limiting ratio; the constants and errors for fixed $j,v$ in Section 3 are used only in that regime. The cited repository comparisons supply the baseline and shared marginal relation, while the original graph-index literature supplies no input theorem for the array extremum proved here. No assertion of literature priority is made.

+**Theorem 4.2 (Unrestricted lower and upper asymptotic bounds).** For every $\kappa\in(0,\infty)$ and every sequence (1.2),
+
+$$
+\max\{0,4\kappa-2\}
+\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}D_n
+\le\limsup_{n\to\infty}D_n
+\le U(\kappa).
+\tag{4.2}
+$$
+
+The infimum defining $D_n$ is over the entire class $\mathcal X(a_n,h_n)$.
+
+**Proof.** Apply Theorem 2.1 with $s=a+1+h$. For every admissible $x$,
+
+$$
+\frac{H(x)-B_0(a)}{a^2}
+\ge\frac{\beta_a(h+1)}{a^2}-2-\frac1a.
+\tag{4.3}
+$$
+
+This bound is uniform over $\mathcal X(a,h)$, so it holds with $H(x)$ replaced by $M(a,h)$. Along (1.2) its right side tends to $4\kappa-2$.
+
+For the other lower bound, reuse [*CDSO incidence moments and capacity phases*, Theorem 11.3](CDSO_INCIDENCE_MOMENTS_AND_CAPACITY_PHASES.md). Its hypotheses hold with $r=a+1\ge5$, $q=a=r-1$ and $s=a+1+h\ge r$. In the notation of that theorem, $2F_{a+1}(a)=a(a+1)^2=B_0(a)$, and $H=2J_s$. Thus $H(x)\ge B_0(a)$ throughout this class, giving $D_n\ge0$. Together these prove the left side of (4.2).
+
+If $0<\kappa\le\sqrt2$, use Proposition 3.2 with $j=1$ and $v=\kappa/\sqrt2\in(0,1]$. Its limiting normalized gap is
+
+$$
+\frac{\kappa^2}{v}+2v=2\sqrt2\,\kappa.
+$$
+
+Since $M(a,h)$ is bounded above by the energy of this actual law, this gives the first upper branch. If $\kappa\ge\sqrt2$, Theorem 3.1 bounds $\limsup D_n$ by $F_j(\kappa)$ for every fixed positive integer $j$. Taking the minimum over these constants proves the second branch. The constructions are available eventually on every sequence (1.2). ∎

+## 1. Common laws and the scalar family

head: 1e621d91eab0a4f07f01af29643201cdc4785056
patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+**Theorem 2.1 (An all-cardinality affine certificate).** Let $a\ge2$ be an integer and $s\ge a$ a finite integer. Let $x$ be any probability law on the nonempty subsets of $[s]$ with $\mathbb E K=a$ and every actual marginal positive. Define $H$ as in Definition 1.1 and put
+
+$$
+\beta_a=4(a-1)\sqrt{a+1}-2a+4.
+\tag{2.1}
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+H(x)\ge a^3+\beta_a(s-a),\qquad
+\frac{\beta_a}{a^{3/2}}\longrightarrow4.
+\tag{2.2}
+$$
+
+This holds for all such laws, including zero type masses, arbitrarily small positive marginals, arbitrary cardinality layers and disconnected incidence support.
+
+**Proof.** The shared-budget inequality in [*CDSO incidence moments and capacity phases*, Theorem 2.2, (2.2)](CDSO_INCIDENCE_MOMENTS_AND_CAPACITY_PHASES.md) gives $U_T\ge K^2/a$. Its common-law calculation is
+
+$$
+\sum_i y_i=\mathbb E K=a,\qquad
+K^2\le\left(\sum_{i\in T}y_i\right)U_T\le aU_T.
+$$
+
+Moreover, summing over the actual inclusion events and using Cauchy–Schwarz within each realized $T$ gives
+
+$$
+\mathbb E U_T=\sum_i\frac{\mathbb P(i\in T)}{y_i}=s,
+\qquad
+K^2\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}\ge K U_T^2.
+\tag{2.3}
+$$
+
+Thus it suffices to bound $\mathbb E(KU_T^2)$ using this same pair $(K,U_T)$.
+
+Write $\beta=\beta_a$ and set
+
+$$
+\lambda=5a^2-2\beta,\qquad \nu=4a^3-a\beta,
+\qquad k_0=(a\beta/2)^{1/3}.
+$$
+
+The inequalities $2a\le\beta\le2a^2$ follow respectively from
+
+$$
+\beta-2a=4(a-1)(\sqrt{a+1}-1)\ge0
+$$
+
+and $2\sqrt{a+1}\le a+2$, whose square is $4a+4\le a^2+4a+4$. Consequently $\lambda>0$, $\nu>0$ and $1\le k_0\le a$. We prove the pointwise inequality
+
+$$
+P(k,u):=ku^2-\lambda k-\beta u+\nu\ge0
+\qquad(k\ge1,\ u\ge k^2/a),
+\tag{2.4}
+$$
+
+where $k$ is allowed to be real.
+
+For $k\ge k_0$, the derivative $2ku-\beta$ is nonnegative on $u\ge k^2/a$, since $2k^3/a\ge\beta$. Hence the minimum on this half-line is at its boundary. With $t=k/a\ge0$, direct factorization gives
+
+$$
+P(k,k^2/a)
+=a^3(t-1)^2\left(t^3+2t^2+3t+4-\frac\beta{a^2}\right)\ge0,
+\tag{2.5}
+$$
+
+because $\beta/a^2\le2$.
+
+For $1\le k\le k_0$, the unconstrained minimizing point $u=\beta/(2k)$ is feasible. Four times $k$ times its value is
+
+$$
+Q(k)=4\nu k-4\lambda k^2-\beta^2.
+$$
+
+This is a concave quadratic. The explicit value (2.1) satisfies
+
+$$
+\beta^2+4(a-2)\beta=16a^3-20a^2,
+$$
+
+so $Q(1)=0$. At $k=k_0$, the unconstrained minimizing point equals $k_0^2/a$, and (2.5) gives $Q(k_0)\ge0$. A concave function lies above the chord joining its endpoint values; therefore $Q(k)\ge0$ throughout $[1,k_0]$. Since $k>0$, this proves (2.4) on the remaining interval.
+
+Apply (2.4) to $(k,u)=(K,U_T)$ and take expectations. By (2.3),
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+H(x)&\ge\mathbb E(KU_T^2)
+\ge\lambda\mathbb E K+\beta\mathbb E U_T-\nu\\
+&=\lambda a+\beta s-\nu
+=a^3+\beta(s-a).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Finally,
+
+$$
+\frac{\beta_a}{a^{3/2}}
+=4(1-a^{-1})\sqrt{1+a^{-1}}
+ -2a^{-1/2}+4a^{-3/2}\longrightarrow4.
+$$
+
+All expectations used the original law. No support reduction or lower bound on its positive marginals was imposed. ∎
+

+**Definition 1.2 (The growing-surplus scale).** A sequence in the growing-surplus regime consists of integers $(a_n,h_n)$ such that
+
+$$
+a_n\ge4,\qquad h_n\ge1,\qquad a_n\longrightarrow\infty,
+\qquad \frac{h_n}{\sqrt{a_n}}\longrightarrow\kappa\in(0,\infty).
+\tag{1.2}
+$$
+
+The normalized infimum along it is
+
+$$
+D_n=\frac{M(a_n,h_n)-B_0(a_n)}{a_n^2}.
+\tag{1.3}
+$$
+
+Subscripts are suppressed when no ambiguity results. Bounds for $\liminf D_n$ and $\limsup D_n$ do not presume convergence, or that different sequences with the same $\kappa$ have a common limit.
+

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+**Definition 5.1 (The one-extra-core-label singleton family).** For integers $a\ge2$, $h\ge1$, partition $[a+1+h]=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$ with $|C|=r=a+1$, $|D|=h$. For the actual parameter domain
+
+$$
+0<\varepsilon\le1/a,
+$$
+
+define
+
+$$
+x_{\{d\}}=\frac\varepsilon h\quad(d\in D),\qquad
+x_C=(a-1)\varepsilon,\qquad
+x_{C\setminus\{i\}}=\frac{1-a\varepsilon}{a+1}\quad(i\in C),
+\tag{5.1}
+$$
+
+and set all other masses to zero. Denote this family by $\mathcal S(a,h)$. At $h=1$ it is the family of [*CDSO incidence moments and capacity phases*, Theorem 10.1](CDSO_INCIDENCE_MOMENTS_AND_CAPACITY_PHASES.md); the tail singleton mass is now split equally over $h$ labels. Its actual marginals and mean are
+
+$$
+y_i=\frac{a-\varepsilon}{a+1}\quad(i\in C),\qquad
+y_d=\frac\varepsilon h\quad(d\in D),\qquad
+\mathbb E K=a.
+$$
+
+Indeed the masses sum to $\varepsilon+(a-1)\varepsilon+1-a\varepsilon=1$, and the mean is $\varepsilon+(a+1)(a-1)\varepsilon+a(1-a\varepsilon)=a$. The parameter domain is exactly the one giving nonnegative displayed masses and positive marginals. Its endpoint $\varepsilon=1/a$ is called the cap. At that endpoint the missing-one types have zero mass, as permitted in Definition 1.1.
+

+**Theorem 4.4 (Matching global limits at every positive even ratio).** For every fixed positive integer $j$ and every sequence of integers with $a_n\to\infty$ and $h_n/\sqrt{a_n}\to2j$,
+
+$$
+\lim_{n\to\infty}
+\frac{M(a_n,h_n)-a_n(a_n+1)^2}{a_n^2}
+=8j-2.
+\tag{4.5}
+$$
+
+In particular this is a limit of the infimum over all actual laws, independent of the chosen sequence at that ratio.
+
+**Proof.** The universal lower bound in Theorem 4.2 is $4(2j)-2=8j-2$. The single law (3.1) with this same fixed $j$ has, by (3.3), limiting normalized gap
+
+$$
+F_j(2j)=\frac{4j^2}{j}+4j-2=8j-2.
+$$
+
+It supplies a matching upper bound for the unrestricted infimum. Squeezing proves (4.5); no finite minimizer is required. ∎
+

head: 1e621d91eab0a4f07f01af29643201cdc4785056
patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+**Theorem 7.4 (Quadratic descent and failure of convex symmetrization).** If $\delta=\lambda/a$ with fixed $0<\lambda<1$, then for all sufficiently large $a$ the choice $\varepsilon=(2r-1)\delta/r^2$ in (7.2) is feasible and
+
+$$
+\mathcal H(\varepsilon)
+=H_d-\frac{8\lambda^2}{a^2}+O_\lambda(a^{-3}).\tag{7.8}
+$$
+
+The remainder and feasibility threshold can be taken uniformly on each compact interval $0<\lambda_-\le\lambda\le\lambda_+<1$. The nonlinear functional $H$ on the full law domain is not convex for any $0<\delta<1/r$.
+
+**Proof.** On each such compact interval the mass upper bound in (7.3) is $(1-\lambda)/a+O(a^{-2})$, whereas $\varepsilon=2\lambda/a^2+O(a^{-3})$ and $\mu=1+O(a^{-1})$. Thus (7.3) holds uniformly eventually. In addition to (7.5), the exact second derivative at zero is
+
+$$
+\mathcal H''(0)
+=4r^2(1+2/a)\mu^{-3}
+ -\frac{24(2r-1)\delta}{a\mu^4}.
+$$
+
+On $0\le z\le\varepsilon$, all denominators in the first three derivatives stay bounded away from zero. Differentiating (7.4) three times therefore gives $\mathcal H'''(z)=O(a^2)$ uniformly on the compact parameter interval. The linear Taylor term at $\varepsilon$ is
+$-16\lambda^2/a^2+O(a^{-3})$, the quadratic term is
+$8\lambda^2/a^2+O(a^{-3})$, and the third-order remainder is $O(a^2\varepsilon^3)=O(a^{-4})$. This proves (7.8).
+
+For the convexity assertion choose any strict descent from Theorem 7.2 and average its law over every label permutation. This average is the fully symmetric mixture of $a$- and $r$-subsets from Lemma 1.2 and has energy $H_d$. Every law being averaged has the same smaller energy $\mathcal H(\varepsilon)$. A convex functional would give $H_d\le\mathcal H(\varepsilon)$, a contradiction. This argument uses actual feasible laws and does not treat the $w_i$ and $y_i$ as independent variables. ∎
+

+**Theorem 3.1 (An integer enlargement of the core).** For integers $a\ge2$, $j\ge1$ and $h\ge j$, put
+
+$$
+m=a+j,\qquad n=h+1-j,\qquad s=m+n=a+1+h.
+$$
+
+Partition $[s]=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$ with $|C|=m$ and $|D|=n$. The single law
+
+$$
+p=\frac{j}{a+j-1},\qquad
+x_C=1-p,\qquad x_{\{d\}}=\frac pn\quad(d\in D),
+\qquad x_T=0\text{ for every other }T
+\tag{3.1}
+$$
+
+has mean cardinality $a$, positive actual marginals and energy
+
+$$
+H_j(a,h)
+=\frac{(a+j)^3(a+j-1)}{a-1}
+ +\frac{(h+1-j)^2(a+j-1)}j.
+\tag{3.2}
+$$
+
+For every fixed positive integer $j$ and every sequence (1.2), this law is admissible eventually and
+
+$$
+\frac{H_j(a_n,h_n)-B_0(a_n)}{a_n^2}
+\longrightarrow F_j(\kappa):=\frac{\kappa^2}j+4j-2.
+\tag{3.3}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** The integers $m,n$ are positive and $0<p<1$. The masses sum to one, and
+
+$$
+\mathbb E K=(1-p)m+p=a.
+$$
+
+Every core marginal is $y_i=1-p=(a-1)/(a+j-1)>0$ and every tail marginal is $y_d=p/n>0$. On the core event the contribution to $H$ is $m^3/(1-p)$; the singleton events contribute $n^2/p$ in total. This proves (3.2), directly from one law.
+
+For fixed $j$,
+
+$$
+\frac{(a+j)^3(a+j-1)}{a-1}
+=(a+j)^3\left(1+\frac j{a-1}\right)
+=a^3+4ja^2+O_j(a).
+$$
+
+Also $n/\sqrt a\to\kappa$ and $(a+j-1)/a\to1$, whence the second term of (3.2), divided by $a^2$, tends to $\kappa^2/j$. Subtract $B_0(a)=a^3+2a^2+a$ to obtain (3.3). Since (1.2) implies $h_n\to\infty$, the condition $h_n\ge j$ holds eventually. The core and the tail singletons lie in separate support components, which are permitted by Definition 1.1. ∎
+

@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+**Proposition 5.2 (A sufficient and necessary cap criterion within this family).** For $a\ge2$ and $h\ge1$, set
+
+$$
+\Gamma_a=\frac{2a^3+2a^2+2a+1}{(a-1)^2}.
+$$
+
+The scalar minimum over the entire actual family $\mathcal S(a,h)$ is at its cap if and only if $h^2\ge\Gamma_a$. In that case it is unique in the parameter and has energy
+
+$$
+\min_{x\in\mathcal S(a,h)}H(x)
+=\frac{a(a+1)^3}{a-1}+ah^2.
+\tag{5.2}
+$$
+
+For every sequence (1.2) with $\kappa>\sqrt2$, the cap condition holds eventually and
+
+$$
+\frac{\min_{x\in\mathcal S(a_n,h_n)}H(x)-B_0(a_n)}{a_n^2}
+\longrightarrow\kappa^2+2.
+\tag{5.3}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Direct summation in (5.1) gives energy
+
+$$
+\phi_{a,h}(\varepsilon)=C_a(\varepsilon)+\frac{h^2}\varepsilon,
+\qquad
+C_a(\varepsilon)=\frac{a^2r^2}{a-\varepsilon}
+ +\frac{V\varepsilon}{(a-\varepsilon)^2},
+\qquad V=(2a+1)(a-1)r^3>0.
+\tag{5.4}
+$$
+
+For example the equivalent expression
+
+$$
+C_a(\varepsilon)
+=\frac{r^2[a^3+(2a^3-2a-1)\varepsilon]}{(a-\varepsilon)^2}
+$$
+
+follows by expansion and is the core term in the energy of Theorem 10.1 cited above. Only the singleton term changes from $1/\varepsilon$ to $h^2/\varepsilon$.
+
+On $0<\varepsilon\le1/a$, all denominators in (5.4) are positive and
+
+$$
+\phi_{a,h}''(\varepsilon)
+=\frac{2h^2}{\varepsilon^3}
+ +\frac{2a^2r^2}{(a-\varepsilon)^3}
+ +\frac{V(4a+2\varepsilon)}{(a-\varepsilon)^4}>0.
+$$
+
+Thus the derivative is strictly increasing. At the cap, differentiation of (5.4) gives
+
+$$
+\phi_{a,h}'(1/a)=a^2(\Gamma_a-h^2).
+\tag{5.5}
+$$
+
+If this is nonpositive, the derivative is negative everywhere to the left of the cap, so the cap is the unique minimum. If it is positive, values immediately to the left are smaller, so the cap cannot minimize. In this latter case $\phi_{a,h}'(\varepsilon)\to-\infty$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and strict convexity gives a unique interior minimum. This also establishes existence of the scalar minimum on its half-open actual domain.
+
+At the cap the core is the full set of size $a+1$ with probability $(a-1)/a$, giving core energy $a(a+1)^3/(a-1)$ and tail energy $ah^2$. This proves (5.2). Since $\Gamma_a/a\to2$ and $h_n^2/a_n\to\kappa^2>2$, the cap criterion holds eventually along the sequences under consideration. Finally
+
+$$
+\frac{a(a+1)^3/(a-1)-a(a+1)^2}{a^2}
+=\frac{2(a+1)^2}{a(a-1)}\longrightarrow2,
+\qquad \frac{ah^2}{a^2}\longrightarrow\kappa^2,
+$$
+
+which proves (5.3). ∎
+

+## 11. The sharp dense improvement on the entire law domain
+
+**Definition 11.1 (Dense infimum and centered incidence).** Retain Definition 1.1, with no restriction on the cardinalities of positive-mass types, and the notation of Definition 7.1. For $0<\delta\le1$ define
+
+$$
+\mathscr D_a(\delta)
+=\inf\{H(x):x\text{ satisfies Definition 1.1 and }\min_i y_i\ge\tau\}.
+\tag{11.1}
+$$
+
+The additional condition in (11.1) defines the dense part of the original domain; it imposes neither exchangeability nor a prescribed support. For a vector $v\in\mathbb R^s$ let
+
+$$
+\Pi v=v-\frac1s\Bigl(\sum_i v_i\Bigr)\mathbf1,
+\qquad \|v\|^2=\sum_i v_i^2.
+$$
+
+For each actual law put
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+z&=r-K,\qquad
+\Phi(z)=z(z-1)(3r-z-1),\\
+\Delta&=\mathbb E K^3-Z,\qquad
+d_i=y_i-\mu,\qquad V=\|d\|^2,\\
+c_i&=\mathbb E[(K^2-r^2)I_i],\qquad c^\circ=\Pi c,\\
+\kappa&=\sqrt{\frac{2a}{s}},\qquad
+A=\kappa(2r-1)\delta,\\
+Q_*&=\frac{A^2}{r^2\mu^3}
+=\frac{2a}{s}\frac{(2r-1)^2\delta^2}{r^2\mu^3}.
+\end{aligned}\tag{11.2}
+$$
+
+Every expectation in these definitions is taken under the same $x$. The reference moment $Z$ is still the adjacent-cardinality moment, rather than an imposed third moment. The polynomial deficit in Lemma 3.1, the centered identity (8.7), and the actual comparison laws (7.2) will be used below. The optimization of feasible joint moments and the distinction between tight bounds and attained bounds have the classical background of D. Bertsimas and I. Popescu, *Optimal inequalities in probability theory: A convex optimization approach*, SIAM J. Optim. 15(3), 780–804, DOI [10.1137/S1052623401399903](https://doi.org/10.1137/S1052623401399903), pp.780–781. The nonlinear dense estimate here is a repo-derived consequence of the actual incidence relation proved below; it is not an application of a theorem optimizing the moment coordinates independently.
+
+**Proposition 11.2 (A centered incidence constraint from the actual law).** Every law of Definition 1.1 satisfies
+
+$$
+\Delta=\mathbb E\Phi(z)\ge0,
+\qquad \boxed{\ \|c^\circ\|\le A+3\Delta.\ }
+\tag{11.3}
+$$
+
+Neither density nor an energy sublevel is assumed.
+
+**Proof.** The secant residual of $k^3$ at $k=a,r$ is
+
+$$
+(k-a)(k-r)(k+a+r)
+=k^3-(a^2+ar+r^2)k+ar(a+r).
+$$
+
+Its expectation is $\mathbb E K^3-Z$, because the actual mean and the reference mean both equal $q$. Substitution $k=r-z$ gives $\Phi(z)$, the deficit already used in (3.3). Its value at $z=-1$ is $6r$, its values at $z=0,1$ vanish, and it is positive for integers $2\le z\le r-1$. This proves the first assertion on every allowed cardinality $1\le K\le s$.
+
+Linearity of projection gives the same-law identity
+
+$$
+c^\circ=\mathbb E\left[(K^2-r^2)
+ \left(I-\frac Ks\mathbf1\right)\right],
+\qquad
+\left\|\mathbf1_T-\frac{|T|}{s}\mathbf1\right\|^2
+=\frac{|T|(s-|T|)}s.
+\tag{11.4}
+$$
+
+Write $p_j=\mathbb P(z=j)$. At $z=-1$ the projected incidence vector is zero, and at $z=0$ the multiplier $K^2-r^2$ is zero. At $z=1$, the norm of each integrand in (11.4) is $(2r-1)\kappa$. For $2\le z\le r-1$, the ratio of its norm to $\Phi(z)$ is
+
+$$
+\frac{(2r-z)\sqrt{(r-z)(z+1)/s}}
+ {(z-1)(3r-z-1)}
+\le\frac{\sqrt{z+1}}{z-1}\le2.
+\tag{11.5}
+$$
+
+Here $2r-z\le3r-z-1$ and $(r-z)/s\le1$; the last inequality follows from $z+1\le4(z-1)^2$ for integers $z\ge2$. The total contribution of these cardinalities therefore has norm at most $2\Delta$. Finally $\mathbb E z=\delta$ implies
+
+$$
+p_1=\delta+p_{-1}-\sum_{j\ge2}j p_j
+\le\delta+\frac{\Delta}{6r}.
+$$
+
+The triangle inequality in (11.4) now gives
+
+$$
+\|c^\circ\|\le(2r-1)\kappa p_1+2\Delta
+\le A+\left(2+\frac{\kappa(2r-1)}{6r}\right)\Delta
+\le A+3\Delta.
+$$
+
+The last coefficient bound uses $\kappa\le\sqrt2$. Thus both the vector being bounded and the deficit paying for all other cardinalities come from the original law. ∎
+
+**Lemma 11.3 (Dense sublevel localization retaining the moment deficit).** Fix $L>0$. For all sufficiently large $a$, uniformly over $0<\delta\le L/a$, every actual dense law with $H\le H_d$ satisfies
+
+$$
+\sqrt V\le\frac{24\delta}{r\mu^3},\qquad
+0\le\Delta\le72\delta^2\mu^{-6},\qquad
+\max_i|c_i|=O_L(r\delta).
+\tag{11.6}
+$$
+
+In particular $y_i=\mu+O_L(\delta/r)$ for every label. These are consequences for this sublevel and are not extra assumptions on the law domain.
+
+**Proof.** Set $R_i=c_i+b$, as in Lemma 3.1. Its pointwise nonnegative residual is
+
+$$
+(1-I_i)(2r+1)(r-K)+I_i(s-K)(s-K-1).
+$$
+
+Consequently
+
+$$
+R_i\ge0,\qquad
+\sum_iR_i=S_0+\Delta,\qquad S_0=6r\delta.
+\tag{11.7}
+$$
+
+The sum identity follows from $\sum_i c_i=\mathbb E K^3-r^2q$ and $Z-r^2q+sb=6r\delta$. With $f(y)=r^2/y-b/y^2$, (8.6)–(8.8) give, for all sufficiently large $a$ in the stated window,
+
+$$
+H=\sum_i f(y_i)+\sum_i\frac{R_i}{y_i^2},\qquad
+\sum_i f(y_i)\ge sf(\mu)+\frac{r^2}{2}V,
+\qquad sf(\mu)+\frac{S_0}{\mu^2}=H_d.
+$$
+
+Indeed $\mu\ge1/2$ and $b/(r^2\mu)\le1/12$ eventually, and density is exactly the other hypothesis needed in (8.7). Put $M=\max_i y_i$. Since $M\le1$, the inverse-square tangent inequality yields
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\sum_i\frac{R_i}{y_i^2}
+&\ge\frac{S_0+\Delta}{M^2}\\
+&\ge\frac{S_0}{\mu^2}
+ -\frac{2S_0}{\mu^3}(M-\mu)+\Delta\\
+&\ge\frac{S_0}{\mu^2}
+ -\frac{2S_0}{\mu^3}\sqrt V+\Delta.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Thus
+
+$$
+H-H_d\ge\Delta+\frac{r^2}{2}V
+ -12r\delta\mu^{-3}\sqrt V.
+\tag{11.8}
+$$
+
+Under $H\le H_d$, nonnegativity of $\Delta$ first gives the bound for $\sqrt V$ in (11.6). Maximizing $12r\delta\mu^{-3}u-r^2u^2/2$ over $u\ge0$ gives the displayed bound for $\Delta$. Finally (11.7) implies
+$|c_i|\le b+S_0+\Delta=O_L(r\delta)$, since $\delta/r$ is uniformly bounded and tends to zero. ∎
+
+**Theorem 11.4 (Uniform sharp dense infimum with no lower window cutoff).** For every fixed $0<L<1$ there are constants $a_0(L),C_L$ such that, for all integers $a\ge a_0(L)$ and all $0<\delta\le L/a$,
+
+$$
+\boxed{\quad
+\left|\mathscr D_a(\delta)-H_d+Q_*\right|
+\le C_L\frac{\delta^3}{r}.
+\quad}\tag{11.9}
+$$
+
+The dense infimum is attained. In particular, for every compact interval $J\subset(0,1)$, uniformly for $\lambda\in J$,
+
+$$
+\mathscr D_a(\lambda/a)
+=H_d-\frac{8\lambda^2}{a^2}+O_J(a^{-4}).
+\tag{11.10}
+$$
+
+The lower bound in (11.9) holds on the entire dense part of Definition 1.1, including laws with arbitrary positive cardinalities and disconnected support.
+
+**Proof.** First consider a dense law with $H\le H_d$. Lemma 11.3 gives uniform lower bounds on all $y_i$ and $\mu$, as well as $\|d\|=O_L(\delta/r)$. Expand the exact identity
+
+$$
+H=\sum_i\left(\frac{r^2}{y_i}+\frac{c_i}{y_i^2}\right).
+$$
+
+The constant term is $(r^2q+\sum_i c_i)/\mu^2=H_d+\Delta/\mu^2$. The $r^2$ linear term vanishes because $\sum_i d_i=0$, and $\langle c,d\rangle=\langle c^\circ,d\rangle$. Thus
+
+$$
+H-H_d=\frac{\Delta}{\mu^2}
+ +\mu^{-3}\left(r^2\|d\|^2-2\langle c^\circ,d\rangle\right)
+ +E,\qquad |E|\le C_L\frac{\delta^3}{r}.
+\tag{11.11}
+$$
+
+To justify the error without a factor depending on the number of labels, use the exact scalar identities
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\frac1{\mu+d}-\frac1\mu+\frac d{\mu^2}-\frac{d^2}{\mu^3}
+ &=-\frac{d^3}{\mu^3(\mu+d)},\\
+\frac1{(\mu+d)^2}-\frac1{\mu^2}+\frac{2d}{\mu^3}
+ &=\frac{d^2(3\mu+2d)}{\mu^3(\mu+d)^2}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+They imply
+
+$$
+|E|\le C\left[r^2\sum_i|d_i|^3
+ +(\max_i|c_i|)V\right]
+\le C_L\left(r^2V^{3/2}+r\delta V\right)
+\le C_L\frac{\delta^3}{r}.
+$$
+
+Complete the square in (11.11):
+
+$$
+H-H_d+Q_*
+=\frac{r^2}{\mu^3}\left\|d-\frac{c^\circ}{r^2}\right\|^2
+ +\frac{\Delta}{\mu^2}
+ +\frac{A^2-\|c^\circ\|^2}{r^2\mu^3}+E.
+$$
+
+By Proposition 11.2 the possibly negative norm gap is at least
+$-(6A\Delta+9\Delta^2)/(r^2\mu^3)$. Since
+$A=O(r\delta)$ and $\Delta=O_L(\delta^2)$, uniformly on the stated window and for large $a$,
+
+$$
+\mu^{-2}-\frac{6A+9\Delta}{r^2\mu^3}\ge\frac12.
+$$
+
+We obtain the stronger sublevel stability estimate
+
+$$
+\boxed{\quad
+H-H_d+Q_*\ge\frac\Delta2
+ +\frac{r^2}{\mu^3}\left\|d-\frac{c^\circ}{r^2}\right\|^2
+ -C_L\frac{\delta^3}{r}.
+\quad}\tag{11.12}
+$$
+
+Dropping its nonnegative terms proves the required lower bound for $H\le H_d$; laws with $H>H_d$ satisfy that lower bound automatically.
+
+For a matching actual upper law, fix a pair $P\subset[s]$ and use (7.2), with its labels relabeled to $P$, at
+
+$$
+\varepsilon_*=
+\frac as\frac{(2r-1)\delta}{r^2}.
+\tag{11.13}
+$$
+
+The two missing-one masses on $P$ are $(1-r\delta)/s-\varepsilon_*$, and each missing-one mass off $P$ is $(1+\delta)/s+2\varepsilon_*/a$. For large $a$, the former are positive uniformly over the whole window: $1-r\delta\ge(1-L)/2$, while $\varepsilon_*=O_L(\delta/r)=O_L(a^{-2})$. The masses of cardinality $r$ add to $1-\delta$, and the sole cardinality-$a$ mass is $\delta$ on $[s]\setminus P$. Hence this is an actual probability law of mean $q$. Its marginals are $\mu+\varepsilon_*$ on $P$ and $\mu-2\varepsilon_*/a$ off $P$, so it is dense for all sufficiently large $a$.
+
+For this one law, directly,
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\Delta&=0,\qquad
+c_i=0\ (i\in P),\qquad
+c_j=-(2r-1)\delta\ (j\notin P),\\
+c^\circ&=(2r-1)\delta
+ \left(\mathbf1_P-\frac2s\mathbf1\right),\qquad
+\|c^\circ\|^2=A^2,\qquad d=\frac{c^\circ}{r^2}.
+\end{aligned}\tag{11.14}
+$$
+
+Its explicit vectors satisfy $\|d\|=O_L(\delta/r)$ and $\max_i|c_i|=O(r\delta)$, so the scalar identities proving (11.11) apply to it directly, without assuming its energy lies in a sublevel. Equations (11.11) and (11.14) give $H=H_d-Q_*+O_L(\delta^3/r)$, proving the upper bound. No exact finite-$a$ minimizing property of this family is needed. The feasible dense laws form a nonempty compact subset of the finite probability simplex with $y_i\ge\tau>0$. Continuity of $H$ proves attainment.
+
+Finally put $h=1/a$ and $\delta=\lambda h$. The exact expression (11.2) becomes
+
+$$
+Q_*=\frac{2\lambda^2h^2(2+h)^2(1+2h)^2}
+ {(1+h)^2(1+h-\lambda h^2)^3}.
+\tag{11.15}
+$$
+
+The rational factor multiplying $\lambda^2h^2$ has constant coefficient $8$ and linear coefficient zero: the relative linear coefficient of both its numerator and denominator is $5$. Taylor expansion with denominators bounded away from zero uniformly on $J$ gives
+$Q_*=8\lambda^2h^2+O_J(h^4)$. Also $\delta^3/r=O_J(h^4)$. Substitution in (11.9) proves (11.10). ∎
+
+## 12. Necessary concentration of an omitted pair
+
+**Theorem 12.1 (Structure forced by asymptotically minimizing dense laws).** Let $J$ be a fixed compact interval in $(0,1)$. For each sufficiently large integer $a$, choose $\lambda_a\in J$, set $\delta_a=\lambda_a/a$, and let $x_a$ be any actual dense law satisfying
+
+$$
+H(x_a)-\mathscr D_a(\delta_a)=o(a^{-2}).
+\tag{12.1}
+$$
+
+Then there exist pairs $P_a\subset[s]$ such that
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathbb P_{x_a}(K=a)&=\delta_a+o(a^{-3}),\\
+\mathbb P_{x_a}(K\notin\{a,r\})&=o(a^{-3}),\\
+\mathbb P_{x_a}(T=[s]\setminus P_a\mid K=a)&=1-o(1),\\
+\left\|y-\mu\mathbf1
+ -\frac{(2r-1)\delta_a}{r^2}
+ \left(\mathbf1_{P_a}-\frac2s\mathbf1\right)\right\|
+ &=o(a^{-2}).
+\end{aligned}\tag{12.2}
+$$
+
+All little-oh assertions are along the given sequence $a\to\infty$; $\lambda_a$ need not converge. The conditional law is defined eventually by the first line. This is a necessary asymptotic structure, not a finite-$a$ equality classification or a sufficiency assertion for arbitrary laws satisfying (12.2).
+
+**Proof.** Since $\lambda_a$ stays bounded away from zero, $Q_*$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $a^{-2}$. Theorem 11.4 and (12.1) therefore put $x_a$ in $H<H_d$ eventually. The left side of (11.12) is $o(a^{-2})$, and its error is $O_J(a^{-4})$. Consequently
+
+$$
+\Delta=o(a^{-2}),\qquad
+\left\|d-\frac{c^\circ}{r^2}\right\|=o(a^{-2}).
+\tag{12.3}
+$$
+
+For $z\ge2$, $\Phi(z)\ge2rz(z-1)$, while $\Phi(-1)=6r$. Hence, with $p_j=\mathbb P(z=j)$,
+
+$$
+p_{-1}+\sum_{j\ge2}p_j=O(\Delta/r),\qquad
+\left|p_1-\delta_a\right|
+=\left|p_{-1}-\sum_{j\ge2}j p_j\right|
+=O(\Delta/r).
+$$
+
+These estimates prove the first two lines of (12.2).
+
+Let $e=d-c^\circ/r^2$. Rewriting (11.11) gives
+
+$$
+H-H_d=-\frac{\|c^\circ\|^2}{r^2\mu^3}
+ +\frac\Delta{\mu^2}+\frac{r^2}{\mu^3}\|e\|^2+E.
+$$
+
+Equations (12.1), (12.3) and Theorem 11.4 imply
+
+$$
+\|c^\circ\|^2=A^2+o(1).
+\tag{12.4}
+$$
+
+Write $p=\mathbb P(K=a)$ and
+
+$$
+v=\mathbb E\left[I-\frac as\mathbf1\ \middle|\ K=a\right].
+$$
+
+The other cardinalities in (11.4) have total projected contribution $O(\Delta)$ by (11.5), and therefore
+
+$$
+c^\circ=-(2r-1)p v+O_{\|\cdot\|}(\Delta).
+\tag{12.5}
+$$
+
+Here $O_{\|\cdot\|}(\Delta)$ denotes a vector of Euclidean norm $O(\Delta)$. The scalar $(2r-1)p$ is bounded above and away from zero, and $p/\delta_a\to1$. Combining (12.4)–(12.5) yields
+$\|v\|^2=\kappa^2-o(1)$, since each centered cardinality-$a$ incidence vector has squared norm $\kappa^2$.
+
+Take independent conditional draws $U,U'$ given $K=a$. The Euclidean variance identity gives
+
+$$
+\mathbb E\|\mathbf1_U-\mathbf1_{U'}\|^2
+=2(\kappa^2-\|v\|^2)=o(1).
+$$
+
+Two distinct $a$-subsets have squared incidence distance at least two. Thus their conditional coincidence probability tends to one. If $\pi_U=\mathbb P(T=U\mid K=a)$, then
+
+$$
+1-o(1)=\sum_U\pi_U^2\le\max_U\pi_U\le1.
+$$
+
+Choose a largest atom $U_a=[s]\setminus P_a$. This proves the third line of (12.2). Since all the centered incidence vectors have norm $\kappa\le\sqrt2$, their mean differs from the vector at this atom by norm at most $2\sqrt2(1-\pi_{U_a})=o(1)$. Hence
+
+$$
+v=\mathbf1_{[s]\setminus P_a}-\frac as\mathbf1+o_{\|\cdot\|}(1).
+$$
+
+Equation (12.5) and $p=\delta_a+o(a^{-3})$ now give
+
+$$
+c^\circ=(2r-1)\delta_a
+ \left(\mathbf1_{P_a}-\frac2s\mathbf1\right)+o_{\|\cdot\|}(1).
+$$
+
+Together with (12.3) this proves the final line of (12.2). In particular the two enhanced marginals and the concentrated omitted pair are properties of the same actual law. ∎
+
+## 13. The sixth competition scale and its fixed critical sequence
+
+**Theorem 13.1 (Sixth-scale competition and eventual phases).** Fix $\eta\in\mathbb R$ and put
+
+$$
+\delta_a=\frac1{2a}-\frac1{a^2}+\frac5{4a^3}
+ -\frac5{4a^4}+\frac\eta{a^5}.
+\tag{13.1}
+$$
+
+These parameters are positive and admissible for all sufficiently large $a$, and
+
+$$
+\boxed{\quad
+\lim_{a\to\infty}a^2
+ \left[D_a(\delta_a)-2a^2-5a-2-\frac7{2a}\right]
+=\min\left\{-\frac{17}{2},-1-4\eta\right\}.
+\quad}\tag{13.2}
+$$
+
+If $\eta<15/8$, every globally minimizing law is eventually dense, and
+
+$$
+D_a(\delta_a)=2a^2+5a+2+\frac7{2a}
+ -\frac{17}{2a^2}+\frac{41}{2a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}).
+\tag{13.3}
+$$
+
+If $\eta\ge15/8$, including the fixed value $\eta=15/8$, the global minimum of $H$ is eventually exactly $H_r$. All globally minimizing laws are, up to relabeling,
+
+$$
+x_{\{e\}}=\frac{\delta_a}{a},\qquad
+x_{[s]\setminus\{e\}}=1-\frac{\delta_a}{a},\qquad
+x_T=0\text{ otherwise},
+\tag{13.4}
+$$
+
+and on this side
+
+$$
+D_a(\delta_a)=2a^2+5a+2+\frac7{2a}
+ +\frac{-1-4\eta}{a^2}
+ +\frac{24-14\eta}{a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}).
+\tag{13.5}
+$$
+
+The parameter $\eta$ in these assertions is fixed. Neither an exact finite-$a$ dense optimizer nor an exact crossing curve for parameters moving beyond the specified sequence is determined by this theorem. The conclusions concern precisely the subset-law domain of Definition 1.1 and do not assert realization or optimality at a prescribed finite graph budget.
+
+**Proof.** The parameters (13.1) eventually satisfy $0<\delta_a\le(3/4)/a$, so both Theorem 11.4 and Theorem 9.1 apply. The latter gives the exact rare minimum $H_r$, attained only by (13.4). Dense and rare are an exhaustive partition of the original domain. Thus
+
+$$
+\inf_xH(x)=\min\{\mathscr D_a(\delta_a),H_r\}.
+\tag{13.6}
+$$
+
+Attainment is also provided by Theorem 10.1.
+
+For the required expansions put $h=1/a$, substitute
+$\delta=h/2-h^2+5h^3/4-5h^4/4+\eta h^5$, and define
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+Q_0&=1+h-h\delta,\\
+P_0&=(1+h)^3-\delta(3h+3h^2+h^3),\\
+F&=P_0/Q_0^2,\\
+R&=\frac{(1+h)^3}{1-h\delta}-(1+h)^2F.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+The exact rational identities (10.7) read
+
+$$
+H_d-B=h^{-2}(2+3h)F,\qquad
+H_r-B=\frac1{h\delta}+h^{-3}R.
+\tag{13.7}
+$$
+
+Multiplying the numerator polynomials and the inverse denominator series gives
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+F&=1+h-\frac12h^2+\frac52h^3-7h^4
+ +\frac{67}{4}h^5+O_\eta(h^6),\\
+\frac1{h\delta}
+ &=2h^{-2}+4h^{-1}+3+h
+ +\left(\frac92-4\eta\right)h^2
+ +(14-16\eta)h^3+O_\eta(h^4),\\
+R&=h^2-h^3+\frac52h^4-\frac{11}{2}h^5
+ +(10+2\eta)h^6+O_\eta(h^7).
+\end{aligned}\tag{13.8}
+$$
+
+For example the first series is characterized to the displayed order by
+$Q_0^2F=P_0$; the second by $(h\delta)(h\delta)^{-1}=1$ after factoring $h^2$; and the third follows by substitution of the first into its defining difference. All inverse factors after these powers of $h$ are removed are analytic near zero: $Q_0\to1$, $1-h\delta\to1$, and $\delta/h\to1/2$. Thus the remainders in (13.8) are bounded Taylor remainders for each fixed $\eta$.
+
+Equations (13.7)–(13.8) yield
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+H_d-B&=2a^2+5a+2+\frac7{2a}
+ -\frac{13}{2a^2}+\frac{25}{2a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}),\\
+H_r-B&=2a^2+5a+2+\frac7{2a}
+ +\frac{-1-4\eta}{a^2}
+ +\frac{24-14\eta}{a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}).
+\end{aligned}\tag{13.9}
+$$
+
+In (11.15) the moving parameter is
+$\lambda_a=a\delta_a=1/2-h+5h^2/4-5h^3/4+\eta h^4$. It stays in a fixed compact interval in $(0,1)$, so
+
+$$
+Q_*=8\lambda_a^2h^2+O_\eta(h^4)
+=2h^2-8h^3+O_\eta(h^4),\qquad
+\frac{\delta_a^3}{r}=O_\eta(h^4).
+$$
+
+Theorem 11.4 therefore sharpens the dense branch to
+
+$$
+\mathscr D_a(\delta_a)-B
+=2a^2+5a+2+\frac7{2a}
+ -\frac{17}{2a^2}+\frac{41}{2a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}).
+\tag{13.10}
+$$
+
+Taking the smaller of (13.9) and (13.10) in (13.6) proves (13.2). More precisely,
+
+$$
+H_r-\mathscr D_a(\delta_a)
+=\frac{15/2-4\eta}{a^2}
+ +\frac{7/2-14\eta}{a^3}+O_\eta(a^{-4}).
+\tag{13.11}
+$$
+
+For fixed $\eta<15/8$ the first coefficient is positive, so every rare law has energy strictly greater than the attained dense infimum. This proves (13.3) and the dense assertion. For fixed $\eta>15/8$ it is negative, so the dense region is strictly above $H_r$; Theorem 9.1 then proves (13.4)–(13.5). At the fixed value $\eta=15/8$, the first coefficient vanishes but the second equals $-91/4$. Hence
+
+$$
+H_r-\mathscr D_a(\delta_a)
+=-\frac{91}{4a^3}+O(a^{-4})<0
+$$
+
+for all sufficiently large $a$, giving the same exact rare minimum and equality class. In this case the $a^{-3}$ coefficients of the rare and dense branches are $-9/4$ and $41/2$, respectively. This decides the stated fixed critical sequence without determining a general finite-$a$ transition curve. ∎
+

@@ -24,8 +24,29 @@ Order whole packets by paying an affordable loss packet first, and otherwise tak
 
 The motivating source is Damasdi, Frankl, Pach and Palvolgyi, Monochromatic configurations on a circle, arXiv:2504.10687v2, Conjecture 3.1, DOI 10.5070/C6.68671. For that conjecture the substitution is the actual centered source on Fin k, sigma=finRotate k, Q=2^(k-2), and k>=3. The native source geometry and seam recurrence supply all bounds and permutation hypotheses. This settles the complete isolated, same-sign SMALL subcase, with arbitrarily many SMALL positions. The construction may change the order of different LARGE pairs. Sources containing adjacent SMALL labels or SMALL labels of both signs, and full Conjecture 3.1, remain open.
 
+**Theorem 1.2 (Both native cyclic filters and a strict prefix margin).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/IsolatedSmallSource.actualSource_isolated_same_sign_cyclic_completion`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/IsolatedSmallSource.actualSource_isolated_same_sign_cyclic_completion` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For the actual centered source on every physical label Fin k, k>=3 and arbitrary natural t, assume only that all SMALL values have one weak sign and that every SMALL label has a LARGE physical forward successor. One ordering of all labels has every natural take-prefix height h in [0,C], satisfies 28h<13N, ends at zero, is native Legal, and preserves the native forward cyclic order of both its LARGE and its SMALL filtered lists. Here N=2^k-1, Q=2^(k-2), and C=(N-1)/2. The witness is a physical permutation, is duplicate-free and exhausts Fin k. An empty SMALL filter and all-LARGE sources are included. Isolation itself excludes the zero source.
+
+Orient the common SMALL sign positively. The existing isolated_geometry bands show that every SMALL label a has a negative LARGE predecessor n and a positive LARGE predecessor p of n. Choose a physical positive LARGE root of minimum value p0. The label involution tau swaps each such adjacent negative/SMALL pair and fixes the other labels. Traversing the native cycle from the chosen root and mapping tau changes [p,n,a] to [p,a,n], and leaves [p,n] fixed. Scanning these disjoint adjacent pairs proves exact equality of each filtered order before restoring the native cyclic cut. Tau need not commute with the physical successor; no commuting conjugacy is asserted.
+
+Use the corrected integer potential P(i)=2w(i)-w(pred(i)) on SMALL phases, and P(i)=w(i)+N on negative phases or w(i) otherwise. Its successor difference is w(tau(i)). Prefixes therefore telescope to P(phase(j))-p0, including long natural takes and the zero endpoint after k physical steps. The geometry bounds 2N<=7p0, 3p<=N and 6a<N give 0<=P-p0 and 28(P-p0)<13N in all three phase categories. Since N=2C+1, integrality gives the half-strip bound. The potential is attached to physical labels, so repeated values, nonunits and proper numerical periods introduce no extra assumptions.
+
+For a nonpositive SMALL source, apply the construction to its negative and rotate the negated word at a maximum original prefix. Each resulting height is the old height at the cut minus another old prefix height, so it is nonnegative and at most the cut height. The old strict 13N/28 bound therefore transports explicitly, together with both filtered cyclic orders. The negate_rotation_prefix_bound theorem controls every rotated prefix by this cut height.
+
+This strengthens the isolated same-sign subcase motivated by Monochromatic configurations on a circle, arXiv:2504.10687v2. It supplies neither an ordering for arbitrary adjacent SMALL labels nor a resolution of full Circle Conjecture 3.1. The argument and library synthesis make no literature novelty claim.
+

@@ -68,6 +68,18 @@ Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/TwoSmallSource.negate_rotation`
 
 For any integer-valued label word L in [0,C] with total zero, there is a cyclic cut j such that every natural prefix of L.rotate(j), evaluated with the negated weights, is again in [0,C]. Choose an attained minimum of the negated prefix sums. The existing nonnegative_rotate_of_minimum theorem gives the lower bound, while prefix_segment_sum and the original strip give the upper bound. The operation changes only the cyclic starting point and preserves every physical occurrence. Both the two-SMALL completion and the arbitrary-count isolated same-sign SMALL construction consume this same sign-restoration theorem.
 
+**Theorem 1.6 (Controlling the rotated prefixes by the cut height).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/TwoSmallSource.negate_rotation_prefix_bound`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/TwoSmallSource.negate_rotation_prefix_bound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For any integer-valued label word L in [0,C] with total zero, there is a cut j<=L.length for which every natural prefix of the rotated word with negated weights is nonnegative, at most C, and at most the original prefix height at j. A minimum of the negated prefix sums gives the cut. Splitting each rotated prefix at the seam expresses its height as an original prefix height subtracted from the cut height; all original heights are nonnegative. The negate_rotation theorem follows by forgetting the cut-height bound. In the isolated native completion, a strict upper margin on all original prefixes therefore bounds every new prefix, including the empty word, full word and takes beyond the length.
+
 The mathematical source context is Damasdi, Frankl, Pach and Palvolgyi, Monochromatic configurations on a circle, arXiv:2504.10687v2, Conjecture 3.1, DOI 10.5070/C6.68671. This result treats exactly two physical SMALL labels. Arbitrary-defect completion and the full global strict lexicographic exchange remain open.

+                DeclarationHandle.Create("D5/S3/Combinatorics/Circle/TwoSmallSource.negate_rotation_prefix_bound"),
+                H("Controlling the rotated prefixes by the cut height"), StatementSource.WithoutFormula(), AssessedProvenance.FromRepo(),
+                Blocks(Paragraph(Text("For any integer-valued label word L in [0,C] with total zero, there is a cut j<=L.length for which every natural prefix of the rotated word with negated weights is nonnegative, at most C, and at most the original prefix height at j. A minimum of the negated prefix sums gives the cut. Splitting each rotated prefix at the seam expresses its height as an original prefix height subtracted from the cut height; all original heights are nonnegative. The negate_rotation theorem follows by forgetting the cut-height bound. This result treats exactly two physical SMALL labels. Arbitrary-defect completion and the full global strict lexicographic exchange remain open."))), []));

+/-- Swap precisely the negative/SMALL adjacent pairs of physical labels. -/
+private noncomputable def isolatedSwap {α : Type*} (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
+    (w : α → ℤ) (Q : ℤ) (i : α) : α :=
+  if w i < 0 ∧ |w (σ i)| < Q then σ i
+  else if |w i| < Q then σ.symm i else i
+
+/-- The correction on SMALL phases accounts for the adjacent label swap. -/
+private noncomputable def isolatedPotential {α : Type*} (σ : Equiv.Perm α)
+    (w : α → ℤ) (Q N : ℤ) (i : α) : ℤ :=
+  if |w i| < Q then 2 * w i - w (σ.symm i)
+  else w i + if w i < 0 then N else 0
+
+private theorem isolated_predecessors {α : Type*}
+    (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (w : α → ℤ) (Q : ℤ) (hQ : 0 < Q)
+    (hnz : ∀ i, w i ≠ 0)
+    (hs : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → 0 < w i ∧ Q ≤ w (σ i))
+    (hn : ∀ i, w i < 0 → 0 < w (σ i))
+    (hp : ∀ i, Q ≤ w i → w (σ i) < 0) :
+    (∀ i, w i < 0 → Q ≤ w (σ.symm i)) ∧
+    (∀ i, |w i| < Q → w (σ.symm i) < 0) := by
+  have negpred (i : α) (hi : w i < 0) : Q ≤ w (σ.symm i) := by
+    by_contra hh
+    by_cases ht : w (σ.symm i) < 0
+    · have := hn (σ.symm i) ht
+      simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at this
+      omega
+    · have hz := hnz (σ.symm i)
+      have hpos : 0 < w (σ.symm i) := by omega
+      have hsmall : |w (σ.symm i)| < Q := by rw [abs_of_pos hpos]; omega
+      have := (hs (σ.symm i) hsmall).2
+      simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at this
+      omega
+  refine ⟨negpred, ?_⟩
+  intro i hi
+  by_contra hh
+  have hz := hnz (σ.symm i)
+  have hpos : 0 < w (σ.symm i) := by omega
+  by_cases ht : Q ≤ w (σ.symm i)
+  · have := hp (σ.symm i) ht
+    simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at this
+    have := (hs i hi).1
+    omega
+  · have ht' : |w (σ.symm i)| < Q := by rw [abs_of_pos hpos]; omega
+    have := (hs (σ.symm i) ht').2
+    simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at this
+    have := abs_lt.mp hi
+    omega
+
+private theorem isolated_potential_geometry
+    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [Nonempty α]
+    (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (w : α → ℤ) (Q N C : ℤ)
+    (hQ : 2 ≤ Q) (hN : N = 4 * Q - 1) (hC : C = 2 * Q - 1)
+    (hbound : ∀ i, -C ≤ w i ∧ w i ≤ C)
+    (hstep : ∀ i, w (σ i) = doubleStep N (w i))
+    (hsmall : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → 0 ≤ w i)
+    (hisolated : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → Q ≤ |w (σ i)|) :
+    ∃ o : α, Q ≤ w o ∧
+      (∀ i, isolatedSwap σ w Q (isolatedSwap σ w Q i) = i) ∧
+      (∀ i, isolatedPotential σ w Q N (σ i) - isolatedPotential σ w Q N i =
+        w (isolatedSwap σ w Q i)) ∧
+      (∀ i, 0 ≤ isolatedPotential σ w Q N i - w o ∧
+        28 * (isolatedPotential σ w Q N i - w o) < 13 * N) := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨hnz, hs, hn, hp⟩ := isolated_geometry σ w Q N C hQ hN hC
+    hbound hstep hsmall hisolated
+  have hslarge (i : α) (hi : |w i| < Q) : Q ≤ w (σ i) := by
+    have hpos := (hs i hi).1
+    have he := (hs i hi).2.1
+    have hh := hisolated i hi
+    rwa [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w (σ i))] at hh
+  obtain ⟨negpred, smallpred⟩ := isolated_predecessors σ w Q (by omega) hnz
+    (fun i hi => ⟨(hs i hi).1, hslarge i hi⟩)
+    (fun i hi => (hn i hi).2.2) (fun i hi => (hp i hi).2.1)
+  have neglarge (i : α) (hi : w i < 0) : ¬|w i| < Q := by
+    have := (hn i hi).1
+    rw [abs_of_neg hi]
+    omega
+  have rootlarge (i : α) (hi : Q ≤ w i) : ¬|w i| < Q := by
+    rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w i)]
+    omega
+  have hex : ∃ i, Q ≤ w i := by
+    let a : α := Classical.arbitrary α
+    by_cases ha : Q ≤ w a
+    · exact ⟨a, ha⟩
+    by_cases hn' : w a < 0
+    · exact ⟨σ.symm a, negpred a hn'⟩
+    · have hz := hnz a
+      have ha' : |w a| < Q := by rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w a)]; omega
+      exact ⟨σ a, hslarge a ha'⟩
+  let roots : Finset α := Finset.univ.filter (fun i => Q ≤ w i)
+  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hex
+  obtain ⟨o, ho, hmin⟩ := roots.exists_min_image w ⟨a, by simpa [roots] using ha⟩
+  have ho' : Q ≤ w o := by simpa [roots] using ho
+  have hmin' (i : α) (hi : Q ≤ w i) : w o ≤ w i :=
+    hmin i (by simpa [roots] using hi)
+  refine ⟨o, ho', ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro i
+    by_cases hi : |w i| < Q
+    · have hipos := (hs i hi).1
+      have hin := smallpred i hi
+      have hinlarge := neglarge (σ.symm i) hin
+      simp [isolatedSwap, hi, show ¬w i < 0 by omega, hin]
+    · by_cases ht : w i < 0 ∧ |w (σ i)| < Q
+      · have hnextpos := (hs (σ i) ht.2).1
+        simp [isolatedSwap, ht, show ¬w (σ i) < 0 by omega, ht.2]
+      · simp [isolatedSwap, ht, hi]
+  · intro i
+    by_cases hi : |w i| < Q
+    · have hipos := (hs i hi).1
+      have hn' := smallpred i hi
+      have hnlarge := neglarge (σ.symm i) hn'
+      have hsnext := hslarge i hi
+      have he := (hs i hi).2.1
+      have ht := (hn (σ.symm i) hn').2.1
+      simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at ht
+      simp only [isolatedPotential, if_pos hi, if_neg (rootlarge (σ i) hsnext),
+        if_neg (show ¬w (σ i) < 0 by omega), add_zero, isolatedSwap,
+        if_neg (show ¬(w i < 0 ∧ |w (σ i)| < Q) by omega)]
+      omega
+    · by_cases hn' : w i < 0
+      · have he := (hn i hn').2.1
+        have hnextpos := (hn i hn').2.2
+        by_cases ht : |w (σ i)| < Q
+        · simp [isolatedPotential, hi, ht, hn', isolatedSwap]
+          omega
+        · simp only [isolatedPotential, if_neg hi, if_neg ht, if_pos hn',
+            if_neg (show ¬w (σ i) < 0 by omega), add_zero, isolatedSwap,
+            if_neg (show ¬(w i < 0 ∧ |w (σ i)| < Q) by tauto)]
+          omega
+      · have hz := hnz i
+        have hi' : Q ≤ w i := by rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w i)] at hi; omega
+        have hnnext := (hp i hi').2.1
+        have he := (hp i hi').1
+        simp [isolatedPotential, hi, neglarge (σ i) hnnext, hn', hnnext, isolatedSwap]
+        omega
+  · intro i
+    have horoot := hp o ho'
+    by_cases hi : |w i| < Q
+    · have hn' := smallpred i hi
+      have hr := negpred (σ.symm i) hn'
+      have hminr := hmin' (σ.symm (σ.symm i)) hr
+      have he1 := (hn (σ.symm i) hn').2.1
+      have he2 := (hp (σ.symm (σ.symm i)) hr).1
+      have hsmall' := hs i hi
+      simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at he1 he2
+      simp only [isolatedPotential, if_pos hi]
+      constructor <;> omega
+    · by_cases hn' : w i < 0
+      · have hr := negpred i hn'
+        have hminr := hmin' (σ.symm i) hr
+        have he := (hp (σ.symm i) hr)
+        simp only [σ.apply_symm_apply] at he
+        simp only [isolatedPotential, if_neg hi, if_pos hn']
+        constructor <;> omega
+      · have hz := hnz i
+        have hr : Q ≤ w i := by rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w i)] at hi; omega
+        have hminr := hmin' i hr
+        have he := hp i hr
+        simp only [isolatedPotential, if_neg hi, if_neg hn', add_zero]
+        constructor <;> omega
+

+/-- Along a physical successor chain, each moved pair has one label of each
+size. Removing successive pairs proves the two filtered orders separately. -/
+private theorem isolated_swap_chain {α : Type*}
+    (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (w : α → ℤ) (Q : ℤ)
+    (hsmallpos : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → 0 < w i)
+    (hsmallnext : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → ¬|w (σ i)| < Q)
+    (hsmallpred : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → w (σ.symm i) < 0)
+    (fuel : ℕ) (L : List α) (o : α)
+    (hlen : L.length ≤ fuel)
+    (hchain : (L ++ [o]).IsChain (fun i j => σ i = j))
+    (hstart : ∀ a, L.head? = some a → ¬|w a| < Q)
+    (hend : ¬|w o| < Q) :
+    (L.map (isolatedSwap σ w Q)).Perm L ∧
+      (L.map (isolatedSwap σ w Q)).filter (fun i => decide (Q ≤ |w i|)) =
+        L.filter (fun i => decide (Q ≤ |w i|)) ∧
+      (L.map (isolatedSwap σ w Q)).filter (fun i => decide (|w i| < Q)) =
+        L.filter (fun i => decide (|w i| < Q)) := by
+  classical
+  induction fuel generalizing L with
+  | zero =>
+    have : L = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp (by omega)
+    subst L
+    simp
+  | succ fuel ih =>
+    cases L with
+    | nil => simp
+    | cons a tail =>
+      have ha := hstart a rfl
+      by_cases ht : w a < 0 ∧ |w (σ a)| < Q
+      · cases tail with
+        | nil =>
+          have he : σ a = o := (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp hchain).1
+          exact False.elim (hend (he ▸ ht.2))
+        | cons b rest =>
+          have hab : σ a = b := (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp hchain).1
+          have htail := (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp hchain).2
+          have hb : |w b| < Q := hab ▸ ht.2
+          have hbpos := hsmallpos b hb
+          have hta : isolatedSwap σ w Q a = b := by
+            rw [isolatedSwap, if_pos ht, hab]
+          have htb : isolatedSwap σ w Q b = a := by
+            rw [isolatedSwap,
+              if_neg (show ¬(w b < 0 ∧ |w (σ b)| < Q) by omega), if_pos hb,
+              ← hab, σ.symm_apply_apply]
+          have hrchain : (rest ++ [o]).IsChain (fun i j => σ i = j) := by
+            cases rest with
+            | nil => simp
+            | cons c xs => exact (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp htail).2
+          have hrstart : ∀ c, rest.head? = some c → ¬|w c| < Q := by
+            intro c hc
+            cases rest with
+            | nil => simp at hc
+            | cons d xs =>
+              have hdc : d = c := Option.some.inj hc
+              subst c
+              have hbd : σ b = d := (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp htail).1
+              exact hbd ▸ hsmallnext b hb
+          obtain ⟨hrperm, hrlarge, hrsmall⟩ := ih rest (by simp only [List.length_cons] at hlen; omega)
+            hrchain hrstart
+          refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+          · simpa only [List.map_cons, hta, htb] using
+              ((hrperm.cons a).cons b).trans (List.Perm.swap a b rest)
+          · simp only [List.map_cons, hta, htb, List.filter_cons]
+            simp only [show Q ≤ |w a| by omega, show ¬Q ≤ |w b| by omega,
+              decide_true, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false, ite_true]
+            rw [hrlarge]
+          · simp only [List.map_cons, hta, htb, List.filter_cons]
+            simp only [ha, hb, decide_true, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, ite_false, ite_true]
+            rw [hrsmall]
+      · have hta : isolatedSwap σ w Q a = a := by simp [isolatedSwap, ht, ha]
+        have hrchain : (tail ++ [o]).IsChain (fun i j => σ i = j) := by
+          cases tail with
+          | nil => simp
+          | cons b rest => exact (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp hchain).2
+        have hrstart : ∀ b, tail.head? = some b → ¬|w b| < Q := by
+          intro b hb
+          cases tail with
+          | nil => simp at hb
+          | cons c rest =>
+            have hcb : c = b := Option.some.inj hb
+            subst b
+            have hac : σ a = c := (List.isChain_cons_cons.mp hchain).1
+            intro hc
+            have hn := hsmallpred c hc
+            rw [← hac, σ.symm_apply_apply] at hn
+            exact ht ⟨hn, hac.symm ▸ hc⟩
+        obtain ⟨hrperm, hrlarge, hrsmall⟩ := ih tail (by simp only [List.length_cons] at hlen; omega)
+          hrchain hrstart
+        refine ⟨by simpa only [List.map_cons, hta] using hrperm.cons a, ?_, ?_⟩
+        · simp only [List.map_cons, hta, List.filter_cons]
+          rw [hrlarge]
+        · simp only [List.map_cons, hta, List.filter_cons]
+          rw [hrsmall]
+
+
+private theorem isolated_positive_cycle {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k)
+    (w : Fin k → ℤ) (Q N C : ℤ)
+    (hQ : 2 ≤ Q) (hN : N = 4 * Q - 1) (hC : C = 2 * Q - 1)
+    (hbound : ∀ i, -C ≤ w i ∧ w i ≤ C)
+    (hstep : ∀ i, w (finRotate k i) = doubleStep N (w i))
+    (hsmall : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → 0 ≤ w i)
+    (hisolated : ∀ i, |w i| < Q → Q ≤ |w (finRotate k i)|) :
+    ∃ L : List (Fin k), L.Perm (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => i)) ∧
+      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ ((L.take n).map w).sum ∧
+        ((L.take n).map w).sum ≤ C ∧ 28 * ((L.take n).map w).sum < 13 * N) ∧
+      (L.map w).sum = 0 ∧
+      (L.filter (fun i => decide (Q ≤ |w i|))).IsRotated
+        ((List.finRange k).filter (fun i => decide (Q ≤ |w i|))) ∧
+      (L.filter (fun i => decide (|w i| < Q))).IsRotated
+        ((List.finRange k).filter (fun i => decide (|w i| < Q))) := by
+  classical
+  letI : NeZero k := ⟨by omega⟩
+  let σ := finRotate k
+  obtain ⟨o, ho, hinvol, hcob, hb⟩ := isolated_potential_geometry σ w Q N C
+    hQ hN hC hbound hstep hsmall hisolated
+  let φ := phase hk o
+  let τ := isolatedSwap σ w Q
+  let P := isolatedPotential σ w Q N
+  let base := (List.range k).map φ
+  let L := base.map τ
+  have hφ (j : ℕ) : σ (φ j) = φ (j + 1) := by
+    apply Fin.ext
+    simp [σ, φ, phase, finRotate_apply, Fin.val_add, Nat.add_assoc]
+  have hφk : φ k = o := by simp [φ, phase, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt o.isLt]
+  have hφ0 : φ 0 = o := phase_zero hk o
+  have hP0 : P o = w o := by
+    have hpos : 0 < w o := by omega
+    have hlarge : ¬|w o| < Q := by rw [abs_of_pos hpos]; omega
+    simp [P, isolatedPotential, hlarge, show ¬w o < 0 by omega]
+  have htel (n : ℕ) : ((List.range n).map (fun j => w (τ (φ j)))).sum = P (φ n) - w o := by
+    induction n with
+    | zero => simp [hφ0, hP0]
+    | succ n ih =>
+      have he := hcob (φ n)
+      change P (σ (φ n)) - P (φ n) = w (τ (φ n)) at he
+      rw [hφ] at he
+      simp only [List.range_succ, List.map_append, List.map_cons, List.map_nil,
+        List.sum_append, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil, add_zero, ih]
+      omega
+  have hprefix (n : ℕ) : ((L.take n).map w).sum = P (φ (min n k)) - w o := by
+    simpa only [L, base, ← List.map_take, List.take_range, List.map_map,
+      Function.comp_def] using htel (min n k)
+  have htotal : (L.map w).sum = 0 := by
+    have hh := htel k
+    simpa only [hφk, hP0, sub_self, L, base, List.map_map, Function.comp_def] using hh
+  let e : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) := Equiv.addLeft o
+  have hbase : base = List.ofFn e := by
+    change (List.range k).map φ = List.ofFn e
+    rw [List.ofFn_eq_map, ← List.map_coe_finRange_eq_range]
+    simp only [base, List.map_map]
+    apply List.map_congr_left
+    intro i _
+    apply Fin.ext
+    rfl
+  have hbaserot : base = (List.finRange k).rotate o.val := by
+    rw [hbase]
+    apply List.ext_getElem
+    · simp
+    · intro i hi₁ hi₂
+      simp only [List.getElem_ofFn, List.getElem_rotate, List.getElem_finRange,
+        List.length_ofFn, List.length_rotate, List.length_finRange]
+      apply Fin.ext
+      simp [e, Fin.val_add, Nat.add_mod, Nat.add_comm]
+  let swapEquiv : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) :=
+    { toFun := τ, invFun := τ, left_inv := hinvol, right_inv := hinvol }
+  have hperm : L.Perm (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin k => i)) := by
+    change (base.map swapEquiv).Perm _
+    rw [hbase, List.map_ofFn]
+    exact (e.ofFn_comp_perm swapEquiv).trans
+      (by simpa only [Function.comp_def, id_eq] using
+        swapEquiv.ofFn_comp_perm (fun i : Fin k => i))
+  obtain ⟨hnz, hs, hn, hp⟩ := isolated_geometry σ w Q N C hQ hN hC
+    hbound hstep hsmall hisolated
+  have hsnext (i : Fin k) (hi : |w i| < Q) : Q ≤ w (σ i) := by
+    have he := (hs i hi).2.1
+    have hz := (hs i hi).1
+    have hh := hisolated i hi
+    rwa [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w (σ i))] at hh
+  have hpred := (isolated_predecessors σ w Q (by omega) hnz
+    (fun i hi => ⟨(hs i hi).1, hsnext i hi⟩)
+    (fun i hi => (hn i hi).2.2) (fun i hi => (hp i hi).2.1)).2
+  have holarge : ¬|w o| < Q := by rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w o)]; omega
+  have hchain : (base ++ [o]).IsChain (fun i j => σ i = j) := by
+    have he : base ++ [o] = (List.range (k + 1)).map φ := by
+      simp only [List.range_succ, List.map_append, List.map_cons, List.map_nil,
+        hφk, base]
+    rw [he, List.isChain_iff_getElem]
+    intro i hi
+    simpa only [List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range] using hφ i
+  have hhead : base.head? = some o := by
+    simp [base, List.head?_map, List.head?_range, ne_of_gt hk, hφ0]
+  obtain ⟨_, hlarge, hsmallorder⟩ := isolated_swap_chain σ w Q
+    (fun i hi => (hs i hi).1)
+    (fun i hi => by
+      have hh := hsnext i hi
+      rw [abs_of_pos (by omega : 0 < w (σ i))]
+      omega)
+    hpred k base o (by simp [base]) hchain
+    (fun a ha => by have he := hhead.symm.trans ha; exact Option.some.inj he ▸ holarge)
+    holarge
+  refine ⟨L, hperm, ?_, htotal, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro n
+    rw [hprefix]
+    obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := hb (φ (min n k))
+    change 0 ≤ P (φ (min n k)) - w o at hlo
+    change 28 * (P (φ (min n k)) - w o) < 13 * N at hhi
+    change 0 ≤ P (φ (min n k)) - w o ∧
+      P (φ (min n k)) - w o ≤ C ∧
+      28 * (P (φ (min n k)) - w o) < 13 * N
+    exact ⟨hlo, by omega, hhi⟩
+  · change (base.map τ).filter _ ~r _
+    rw [hlarge, hbaserot]
+    exact TwoSmallSource.filter_rotate _ _ _
+  · change (base.map τ).filter _ ~r _
+    rw [hsmallorder, hbaserot]
+    exact TwoSmallSource.filter_rotate _ _ _
+
+/-- Isolated native SMALL labels of one weak sign admit a full physical
+half-strip word with strict 13/28 margin and both forward cyclic filters.
+No assumption on the source's numerical period or SMALL cardinality is used. -/
+theorem actualSource_isolated_same_sign_cyclic_completion
+    {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (t : ℕ)
+    (hsmall : (∀ i : Fin k, |actualSource k t i| < quarter k → 0 ≤ actualSource k t i) ∨
+      (∀ i : Fin k, |actualSource k t i| < quarter k → actualSource k t i ≤ 0))
+    (hisolated : ∀ i : Fin k, |actualSource k t i| < quarter k →
+      quarter k ≤ |actualSource k t (finRotate k i)|) :
+    ∃ L : List (Fin k),
